final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced on 9.12.0 only (already fixed at this revision)

**Expected:** `no-lonely-if` doesn't offer a fix that changes behavior.
**Actual (9.12.0, and also 9.14.0):** it reports `3:9 Unexpected if as the only statement in an else block.` and the autofix turns `else { if (false) {} }` into `else if (false) {}`. After that, the outer `else throw ...` attaches to the inner `if`, so it now runs. Running the fixed code throws "This `else` should have been unreachable!". The original code doesn't throw.
**Current revision (6f37b07, 9.15.0):** nothing is reported, so no fix is applied and the output stays the same as the input. `tests/lib/rules/no-lonely-if.js` passes (17 tests).
**Trigger:** the `if` that owns the lonely-`if` `else` block is itself the unbraced consequent of an outer `if` that has its own `else`.

**Why it's fixed:** commit 9db5b15, "fix: unsafe report for `no-lonely-if` (#19087)", is already in this checkout and listed under v9.15.0 in CHANGELOG.md. It makes the rule skip reporting when `astUtils.areBracesNecessary(parent, sourceCode)` is true. That helper was moved out of `curly`, so `no-lonely-if` now treats these braces the same way `curly` does, which matches what the reporter pointed to. It also adds `if (a) if (a) {} else { if (b) {} } else {}` as a valid test case. I found this commit in the local git log and CHANGELOG only; I didn't open the issue or the PR.

**Run:**
- Fixed at this revision: `node tmp-repro/no-lonely-if-19033.js` prints OK and exits 0.
- Reproduce the bug: `npm i --prefix /tmp/e912 eslint@9.12.0 && ESLINT_PATH=/tmp/e912/node_modules/eslint node tmp-repro/no-lonely-if-19033.js` prints BUG and exits 1.

I didn't change any production code. The only thing I added is the repro script `tmp-repro/no-lonely-if-19033.js`. No further fix is needed on this revision.
